title: Playing for audiences unfamiliar with jazz, such as Africa
summary: He enjoys places he has not been, such as Africa, where communicating musically is a challenge, and finds someone knows jazz almost everywhere.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you about that one trip you had to Africa.
You seem to -- as I recall years ago, when you came back, was very excited about that kind of entry into it.
Oh, it was still a fresh idea to me, and I still enjoyed going to places I haven't been.
What happens then when you go to a place where you're pretty sure that the majority of the people are not familiar with your music and maybe don't even know what this idiom is? What happens?
Well, I think that's one of the great challenges, if you can find a means of communicating with these people musically, I think you're accomplishing something.
And I -- most times we found some sort of way.
Have you found, no matter where you've gone, there are people who (inaudible) who you are?

Almost everywhere in the world, there's somebody who has heard jazz or is involved or is a collector of records, or is in some way or another influenced. And so there's always something going on for you.
